concept_html:
Silver turns deliveries into a dependable table. Its contract:

  • Canonical names. Rename supplier columns to the names in the Variable Registry, loaded at run time.
  • Declared types. Cast each column to the type in the registry.
  • Grain. One row per respondent per wave. Keep the newest delivery version per key, then MERGE (lesson A3-L1).

Two Spark behaviours make the first two steps fail silently or loudly, in the wrong place.

Renames skip missing columns. withColumnRenamed("wgt", "final_weight") does nothing when wgt is absent, and so does withColumnsRenamed. No error, no warning. If the supplier renames wgt to weight, silver loses its weight column, and the failure surfaces hours later in gold. Check the source columns yourself before you rename, and raise one error that lists every missing column.

Casts under ANSI mode. Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS runs Spark 4.0, which turns ANSI mode on by default. cast("abc" as int) now raises CAST_INVALID_INPUT and stops the job at the first bad value. Older runtimes returned NULL without a word. Neither is what you want in silver. Use try_cast, which returns NULL for a bad value, then count the new NULLs and let a data-quality check decide: under 0.1% is a WARN, above it is CRITICAL.

F.col("final_weight").try_cast("double")

The pattern is: check columns, rename, try_cast, count cast failures, deduplicate, MERGE. Each step is a small function you can test.

lines: def require_columns(df: DataFrame, columns: list[str]) -> None:
"""Raise ValueError listing every column missing from df."""
missing = sorted(set(columns) - set(df.columns))
if missing:
raise ValueError(f"missing source columns: {missing}")
def rename_to_canonical(df: DataFrame, column_map: dict[str, str]) -> DataFrame:
"""Rename supplier columns to registry names. Fails on any missing column."""
require_columns(df, list(column_map))
return df.withColumnsRenamed(column_map)
def cast_to_registry_types(df: DataFrame, type_map: dict[str, str]) -> DataFrame:
"""Cast with try_cast, so a bad value becomes NULL instead of stopping the job."""
require_columns(df, list(type_map))
return df.withColumns({c: F.col(c).try_cast(t) for c, t in type_map.items()})
def count_cast_failures(df: DataFrame, type_map: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, int]:
"""Per column, rows whose non-null value fails try_cast. One pass over df."""
failures = [
F.count_if(F.col(c).isNotNull() & F.col(c).try_cast(t).isNull()).alias(c)
for c, t in type_map.items()
]
return df.agg(*failures).collect()[0].asDict()

lines: def transform_to_silver(bronze_df, column_map, type_map, wave_id):
for src, tgt in column_map.items():
bronze_df = bronze_df.withColumnRenamed(src, tgt)
for col_name, col_type in type_map.items():
bronze_df = bronze_df.withColumn(col_name, col(col_name).cast(col_type))
bronze_df = bronze_df.withColumn("wave_id", lit(wave_id))
return bronze_df

wrong_answers.feedback: That was the behaviour before ANSI mode became the default. On Spark 4.0 use `try_cast` to get NULL.
Casting never drops rows. It either raises or returns a value.
Spark never turns malformed text into 0.0. It raises, or with try_cast returns NULL.
Right outcome, wrong reason. Delta accepts NULLs unless a NOT NULL constraint says otherwise. The error comes from the ANSI cast.

exercises.solution:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame


def rename_to_canonical(df: DataFrame, column_map: dict[str, str]) -> DataFrame:
    """Rename supplier columns to registry names.

    Args:
        df: A bronze delivery.
        column_map: Supplier name to canonical name.

    Returns:
        The frame with canonical names.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any source column in column_map is missing from df.
    """
    missing = sorted(set(column_map) - set(df.columns))
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"missing source columns: {missing}")
    return df.withColumnsRenamed(column_map)

title: Silver: canonical names, checked types, one row per respondent per wave
why_html:
A supplier renames wgt to weight without notice. The silver job calls withColumnRenamed("wgt", "final_weight"), which silently does nothing. The type-casting loop skips final_weight because the column is missing. Silver writes the wave with no weight column, since schema evolution is on. At 03:00 the gold job fails with final_weight not found. The morning report shows nothing for the new wave.

A column check before the rename fails the silver job at 01:00 with one clear message: "missing source columns: wgt". The on-call engineer knows exactly what to ask the supplier.
